question.body:
The function $g$ has derivatives of all orders, and the Maclaurin series for $g$ is $ sum_(n = 0)^(oo)(- 1)^(n) frac(x^(2 n + 1),2 n + 3)= frac(x,3)- frac(x^(3),5)+ frac(x^(5),7)- dots.h.c $

(a) Using the ratio test, determine the interval of convergence of the Maclaurin series for $g$.

(b) The Maclaurin series for $g$ evaluated at $x = frac(1,2)$ is an alternating series whose terms decrease in absolute value to 0. The approximation for $g lr((frac(1,2)))$ using the first two nonzero terms of this series is $frac(17,120)$. Show that this approximation differs from $g lr((frac(1,2)))$ by less than $frac(1,200)$.

(c) Write the first three nonzero terms and the general term of the Maclaurin series for $g'(x)$.
